topic: Find your fund's expense ratio and know what's too high
caption:
Every mutual fund charges you for running it, and you will never see a bill. The expense ratio comes out a little each day, before the NAV you look at is published.

The ceiling for an open-ended equity scheme under ₹500 crore is now 2.10% a year, down from 2.25%. Larger schemes are capped lower. A ceiling is not a target — plenty of funds sit well below it.

One thing worth knowing before you compare: from 1 April 2026 the number changed shape. GST, securities transaction tax, stamp duty and exchange fees moved outside the base expense ratio and are charged separately now. So part of the apparent drop is a rearrangement, not a saving. Compare funds with each other today rather than with what the same fund showed last year.

Yours is on the scheme factsheet, on the fund house site and on your account statement. While you are there, check which plan you hold: a direct plan carries no distributor commission, a regular plan does, and the gap is charged every year you stay.

Source: SEBI expense ratio framework effective 1 April 2026, and published industry analyses, October 2026.
For education only. Not investment advice.
